against.text: The central denial is specific: AARO states it found no empirical evidence for claims that the government and private companies have been reverse-engineering extraterrestrial technology, and that none of its interviewees had firsthand knowledge of the programmes they described.

The companies named are on record, by AARO's account: its report states that AARO met executives and chief technology officers of the named companies, and that all denied the existence of the programmes and attested to the truthfulness of their statements on the record.

Where the government has given a specific explanation it is on paper: the Air Force's 1994 report concluded the Roswell wreckage most likely came from a Project Mogul balloon train, and Case Closed attributed the bodies accounts to test dummies and later accidents; AARO reaffirmed the Mogul identification in 2024.
The Navy has acknowledged what it cannot explain: its spokesman stated in September 2019 that the Navy designates the objects in the three released videos as unidentified aerial phenomena.

Some claims the denials answer have themselves been undermined: a 2025 claimant said he found Immaculate Constellation in a folder labelled 2018 Schriever Wargame, and Jason Colavito concluded he had mistaken fictitious wargame documents for real ones. The board notes that this addresses the 2025 claim, not the 2024 document.

The denial of Elizondo's role has held since June 2019: the Department says DIA administered AATIP, Elizondo was never assigned to DIA, and although he interacted with the office running it, he did not lead it; his own account that he ran it rests on his and TTSA's statements.

answer.text: On 7 June 2023 Susan Gough said on the Department's behalf that AARO had not discovered any verifiable information to substantiate claims of programmes possessing or reverse-engineering extraterrestrial materials; after the July 2023 hearing she added that the Department had no information that anyone had been harmed or killed for providing information to AARO.

AARO's Volume I concludes there is no empirical evidence of government or corporate reverse-engineering of extraterrestrial technology, states that AATIP was never an official DoD programme, and records that executives of the named companies all denied such programmes on the record; Pat Ryder presented it as approaching the claims with the widest possible aperture.

On AATIP the statements reverse each other: in May 2019 Christopher Sherwood said AATIP did pursue research into unidentified aerial phenomena; in December 2019 Gough said neither AATIP nor AAWSAP was UAP related; in May 2021 she said the contract allowed research drawn from sources including UAP reports, but that examining them was not its purpose.

Some denials are records assertions: the Department told the press it had no record of any SAP called Immaculate Constellation, former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick has denied that it exists, and on the board's reading a no-record answer is a statement about records rather than a denial that the programme exists.

Denial has also been the required answer to true things: the National Reconnaissance Office's existence was classified for thirty-one years, and the CIA historian Gerald Haines wrote in 1997 that Air Force investigators knowingly gave false explanations to protect U-2 and OXCART flights.

for.text: The Department's own statements disagree: Gough's December 2019 denial reversed Sherwood's May acknowledgement, and her May 2021 statement partly reversed her own. On the board's reading, the one position that never moved was the denial of Elizondo's role.

On the board's reading the Department's own released records cut against its denial of Elizondo's role: September 2017 emails show him drafting a memorandum for Neill Tipton to assume the new responsibilities for AATIP, and he submitted the August 2017 release form for the AATIP-associated videos. On the same reading, the June 2019 statement concedes the programme and his contact with it, and turns on the word assigned.

Volume I states that AARO found no non-disclosure agreements containing UAP information, and the Department later confirmed that Air Force personnel signed NDAs over a fictitious alien-technology programme; the two statements cannot both stand as written. The Yankee Blue account itself comes from the Wall Street Journal, and a Pentagon spokesperson could not confirm the memo it described.

The negative findings are bounded by access: AARO's corporate denials rest on executives' voluntary statements with no inspection of any contractor facility described, and Gough's own February 2026 figures put about 1,000 of more than 2,000 reports in AARO's archive without enough data for analysis, which on the board's reading means the finding rests on the analysed half.

On the board's reading, an office without subpoena power reporting inside the department concerned cannot structurally resolve allegations of concealment within that department, which is how every AARO denial is worded.

AARO has never publicly addressed the Immaculate Constellation name entered into the Congressional Record in either annual report or any PURSUE tranche, and Volume II, which Kosloski said in November 2024 would come within months, was not listed on AARO's own products index as of 12 August 2026.

lead.text: The Department of Defense denies that any programme possessing or reverse-engineering extraterrestrial material has been found, in words that report what AARO has discovered rather than what exists. Read as a dated ledger, its statements on AATIP moved from acknowledgement to flat denial to partial concession, while its denial that Luis Elizondo ran the programme never moved.

open: Why has the Department never produced the AATIP charter or an organisation chart that would settle whether Elizondo led it?
What internal coordination produced the June 2023 statement, and did AARO clear its wording?
How many reports in AARO's archive will ever be analysed, and would the negative finding survive them?
Does the department-level memo on Yankee Blue exist, and when was DNI Haines briefed on it?
When will Volume II of AARO's historical record appear, and will it address the fake Air Force programme it was promised to cover?

threads.text: The denials thread runs eight steps, each joined to the next by a denial rather than a connection. AARO's 2024 review does not mention the Wilson-Davis notes or Admiral Wilson; Volume I states that AARO found no UAP-related NDAs, which the board records as contradicted by the Yankee Blue record; a Pentagon spokesperson could not confirm the Yankee Blue memo; no AARO annual report, statement for the record or PURSUE tranche has addressed Immaculate Constellation, of which the Department says it has no record; the Department told House Oversight staff that only HASC and HAC-D members could be read in; and MITRE conditions any production to Congress on coordination with its sponsoring agencies.
